clock_dir_past: "tar éis" (after, past) counts UP from the named hour: "leathuair tar éis
a trí" is 03:30 and "ceathrú tar éis a trí" is 03:15.  Ulster substitutes
bitesize.irish "How To Say What Time It Is in Irish".
clock_dir_to: "chun" (to) counts DOWN to the named hour: "ceathrú chun a dó" is 01:45.
clock_fraction_15: "ceathrú" (a quarter, of an hour), which likewise takes its direction from
clock_fraction_30: "leathuair" (half-hour), which takes its direction from "tar éis"/"chun"
and never stands bare: "leathuair tar éis a trí" is 03:30, an hour LATER
than the toward-the-coming-hour reading some of Irish's neighbours use.
clock_meridiem_am: Unicode CLDR 47, locale ga, gregorian calendar: the am marker.
clock_meridiem_pm: Unicode CLDR 47, locale ga, gregorian calendar: the pm marker.
marker_article: The definite article, singular "an" and plural "na".
marker_at: The particle "a" that introduces a clock hour: "a trí a chlog" (three
o'clock), "a haon a chlog" (one o'clock).  The hour after it is the
DISJUNCTIVE cardinal, never the counting form.  Source: omniglot.com
"Time in Irish"; bitesize.irish "How To Say What Time It Is in Irish".
The same particle enumerates: "uimhir a 3" is number 3 and "seomra a 5" is
room 5, neither of them a time.  Nothing in the surface tells the two uses
apart, so the clock orders that read this particle all require corroborating
clock context -- "a chlog", a meridiem, or a fraction and its direction.
marker_between: "idir" (between), paired with "agus".  In its plain spatial and temporal
sense it leaves both bounds unmutated ("idir Corcaigh agus Gaillimh"); the
separate "both ... and ..." sense that lenites them is not a date range and
is not read here.  Source: en.wiktionary.org, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/idir
marker_every: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/gach.  Only the unmarked collocation is read:
"gach" imposes h-prothesis on some following nouns and lenition on others
with no rule any source states, so no mutated surface is listed for it.
marker_for: "ar feadh" (for, over a period of time): "ar feadh trí lá" (for three
days).  It governs the genitive and mutates nothing itself.  Source:
marker_from: "ó" (from, since): "ó Luan seo chugainn" (from next Monday).  Source:
marker_in: The locative preposition "i" (in), which eclipses the month name that
follows it ("i mBealtaine"); "in" is its form before a vowel.
marker_last: "seo caite" (last), glossed for nouns denoting a period of time and
marker_minute_word: The minute noun spoken between a count and a clock direction: "deich
nóiméad tar éis a hocht" (ten past eight).
marker_next: "seo chugainn" (next), glossed for nouns denoting a period of time and
TRAILING the noun: "an Luan seo chugainn" (next Monday).  Source:
marker_past: "ó shin" (ago), an adverb that TRAILS the quantity it counts back:
"cúig lá ó shin" (five days ago).  Source: en.wiktionary.org,
marker_this: "seo" (this), the demonstrative the two period markers above are built on.
marker_to: "go dtí" closes a range as well as an open bound.
marker_until: "go dtí" (until, up to): "tá sé dúnta go dtí an Luan" (it is closed until

unit1_second: Singular only: the form a count of one, spoken or unspoken, takes.
unit1_year: The lenited "bhliain" is the singular the numeral two imposes.
unit_day: "lá" begins with a consonant the modern standard spells no lenition on, so
the counted phrase shows the radical throughout: "ar feadh trí lá" (for
three days) is the attested worked example on en.wiktionary.org "ar feadh".
unit_hour: The counted plural is the irregular "uaire", which the same entry's usage
note gives with its mutations spelled out -- h-prothesis after three to
six ("trí huaire", "cúig huaire") and eclipsis after seven to ten
("seacht n-uaire").  Both mutated surfaces are listed, so a counted phrase
matches whichever the numeral before it imposes.
unit_minute: (m., 1st declension: genitive singular and nominative plural "nóiméid").
No counted form after a numeral is attested for this noun.
unit_month: The lenited "mhí" is the form of the same entry's mutation table, and the
one the attested "ar feadh trí mhí" (for three months) shows.
unit_second: No counted form after a numeral is attested for this noun, so none is
listed and a mutated surface for it is not read.
unit_week: No counted form after a numeral is attested for this noun.
